title: Browser sexagesimal conversion loses the sign below one degree
summary: `indigo_server/resource/indigo.js:462-490`: dtos truncates signed degrees with `d | 0`, losing the minus sign when -1 < value <0. stod determines the sign using `parseInt(degrees) <0`, which is false for negative zero. Actual Node execution of the committed functions returned `dtos(-0.5) == "0:30:00"` and `stod("-0:30:00") == +0.5`. `components.js:1124-1184` uses these functions for sexagesimal editing/display, and generic property controls use them at1418/1426/1445. `mount.html` uses those controls and dtos for picked target coordinates. Declinations/latitudes just south of zero can therefore be displayed or sent north of zero. Remediation:  Full evidence: C-03. Remediation: preserve the original sign separately from integer degree magnitude in formatting and parse the leading string sign; test positive/negative sub-degree values, zero, nonzero integer degrees and round-trip precision in ordinary coordinate widgets.
evidence: core-functional-review.md section C-03; exact source and ordinary functional proof retained there.

resolution.evidence: 20261025211159-e308-fix-audit-findings-batch/verification.md and group-reports.md: 664f00402: indigo.js dtos/stod keep the sign below one degree; test-indigo-js-formatting pass.
